title: Introduce segregated-slab allocator and deferred eviction windows for KV cache
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a segregated-slab allocator with per-tenant memory segments and a deferred-eviction window to the KV cache. Reduces fragmentation and eviction churn; improves tail latency under mixed workloads. Backwards-compatible, rollout via feature flag and staged canary.
description:
Context and motivation: we continue to see suboptimal tail latencies and sudden spikes in CPU due to aggressive immediate evictions from the KV cache under mixed workloads (short prompt bursts + long-chat sessions). Previous work looked at spillover and compaction; this change takes a complementary approach: reduce cross-tenant fragmentation and eviction churn by separating memory into size-classed, tenant-segmented slabs and by batching reclamation via a short deferred-eviction window.

Goals: 1) lower median and tail LAT for token-level hot paths, 2) reduce CPU pressure from nonstop eviction churn, 3) lower long-lived fragmentation and reduce the frequency of heavyweight compaction.

High-level design:
- Segregated slab allocator: size classes for small/medium/large KV entries with per-tenant segments. Each tenant gets soft-reserved slabs; freelists are local to segments to improve cache locality and avoid global locking. The allocator is written in Rust and exposes a C API to the runtime.
- Deferred eviction windows: instead of immediately freeing entries that are evicted by LRU/TTL, we place them into a deferred window (configurable N ms). During this window, hot re-accesses can be promoted back into the active set without incurring expensive reallocation. A background reclamation worker drains the window in batches and performs low-impact compaction when fragmentation watermarks are hit.
- Cooperative eviction backoff: the eviction path now signals the scheduler to prefer colocated slots for hot shard processing, reducing remote migration. Evictions that would produce high fragmentation are delayed with an adaptive backoff.
- Passive lane compactor: a low-priority background compactor walks per-segment free lists and compacts only when fragmentation_ratio > threshold (default 0.28). This avoids frequent global compaction runs.
- Observability and flags: added fragmentation_ratio, deferred_evictions, deferred_window_ms, per-tenant_segment_usage, reallocation_hits, and eviction_backoff_count metrics; runtime flags for feature rollout: KV_SEGREGATED_SLAB=true/false, KV_DEFER_WINDOW_MS=100 (default), KV_PASSIVE_COMPACTOR=true.

Implementation notes:
- New files: runtime/kv/segregated_slab.rs, runtime/kv/deferred_eviction.rs, runtime/kv/segment_manager.rs, runtime/scheduler/tenant_affinity.rs, observability/metrics/kv_frag.prom.
- API contract: allocator is a drop-in replacement for the previous arena with identical external semantics except for the new flags and metrics.
- Memory safety: thorough checking for ABA using epoch counters on freelists; unit tests for double-free and dangling access.
- Rollout: staged canary by tenant; default disabled. Feature gate metadata added to console so SRE can flip per-region.

Performance summary: in microbenchmarks (mixed small 80% + large 20% request mix) on a 16GB KV cache config:
- fragmentation_ratio reduced from 0.54 -> 0.16 after 30m steady-state
- median token-serving latency improved by ~15%
- 95th percentile token-serving latency improved by ~21%
- background CPU for evictions down ~32%

Integration test plan:
- new tests under tests/kv/cover_deferred_evictions.go exercise reaccess during deferred window
- fragmentation integration test simulates long-running mixed workload and validates passive compactor triggers
- benchmark harness extended under benchmark-lab/kv_frag to produce reproducible numbers

Quick snippet (allocator API usage): "let handle = SegSlab::alloc(size_class, tenant_id); // returns KV handle; free enqueues into deferred window"

Compatibility and caveats:
- Because slabs are per-tenant, hotspots may exhaust their soft-reserved slabs and then borrow from the global pool; borrowing is instrumented and visible via per-tenant metrics.
- Deferred window trades a small, bounded memory overhead for lower churn; default window (100ms) was chosen empirically.
- This PR does not change disk-based spillover behavior; it is complementary.

Rollout steps included in this PR: feature flag flip disabled by default -> enable for 5% tenants -> monitor metrics (deferred_evictions, fragmentation_ratio, tail latency) -> 25% -> 100%.

Linked follow-ups: ENG-7490 (optimize cross-shard relocation when borrowing), ENG-7556 (disk-backed deferred spill buffer).
